title: Landforms, Rocks and Minerals
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Landforms, Rocks and Minerals Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Rocks are made of minerals; rocks are igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic; minerals have properties such as hardness, luster and color; rocks and minerals are used by people; landforms are shaped by rocks. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): rocks and minerals, properties of minerals, how rocks form, uses of rocks and minerals and rock layers and investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Igneous rocks cool from magma; sedimentary rocks form in layers; metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rocks are made of one or more minerals. Minerals are natural, non-living solids.

  • Minerals are identified by hardness (Mohs scale, talc 1 to diamond 10), color, streak and lustre.
  • Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools (granite, basalt).
  • Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment pressed together (sandstone, limestone) and may hold fossils.
  • Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change rocks (marble, slate).
Example

A mineral scratches quartz. What do you know?

harder minerals scratch softer ones

Answer: it is harder than quartz

Example

Which rock type might have fossils?

fossils form in sediment layers

Answer: sedimentary

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a mineral's outside color always matches its streak.
  • Mixing up rocks and minerals.
  • Thinking fossils are found in igneous rocks.

faq.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
faq.a: A mineral is one natural solid substance. A rock is made of one or more minerals.

faq.q: How do we test the hardness of a mineral?
faq.a: Try to scratch it with objects of known hardness, such as a fingernail, a copper coin, a steel nail and glass.

faq.q: Why is mining important in the Philippines?
faq.a: The Philippines mines nickel, gold and copper, but mines must be managed and cleaned up to protect forests, rivers and people.

Streak shows how heavy a mineral is.

from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together

items.q: Gypsum is 2 on the Mohs scale. Can a fingernail (about 2.5) scratch it?
c: Yes, because the fingernail is harder.
items.e: A harder object scratches a softer one.

items.q: What is lustre?

items.e: Lustre can be metallic, glassy or dull.

The area was once covered by water.
items.e: A tree leaf fossil is evidence that the area was once dry land with plants or animals living on it.

items.q: The rock layers have not been turned over. Which layer formed most recently?
items.e: The top layer (A) formed last, so it is the youngest.

items.q: Kenneth sees the same three layers in two cliffs across a valley. What can he conclude?
c: The layers are different ages on each side.
The cliffs formed in different places.

The valley is older than the layers.
items.e: Matching patterns show the layers formed together.

items.q: Which fossil is older: the coral or the fern?
c: the one closer to the top
items.e: The coral is in a lower layer, so it is older.

items.q: Fossil seashells are found high in the hills. What does this tell us?
c: The land was once under the sea.
items.e: Fossils are clues.

items.q: Which fossil is older: the seashell or the shark tooth?
c: the one closer to the top
items.e: The shark tooth is in a lower layer, so it is older.

items.q: Why does pumice float on water?
c: It is full of tiny holes filled with air.
items.e: Gas bubbles were trapped as lava cooled.

items.q: A rock fizzes when a drop of vinegar is put on it. Which rock could it be?
items.e: Acid reacts with chalk and limestone.

items.q: The rock layers have not been turned over. Which layer is older, layer A or layer E?
items.e: Layer E is lower than layer A, so it is older.

items.q: Which fossil is older: the clam or the shark tooth?
c: the one closer to the top
items.e: The clam is in a lower layer, so it is older.

items.q: Why would chalk be a poor choice for a doorstep?

items.e: Choose hard rock for steps.

items.q: The bottom layer has a clam fossil. The top layer has a dinosaur footprint fossil. How did this area change over time?
c: It was dry land first and later became covered by ocean.
Both layers formed on the same day.
It was covered by ocean first and later became dry land.
items.e: Bottom layers are older. The clam (older) shows covered by ocean; the dinosaur footprint (younger) shows dry land.

items.q: Why are there so few fossils of jellyfish?
c: Jellyfish have no hard parts, so they usually rot away.
items.e: Hard parts last.

items.q: The bottom layer has a tree leaf fossil. The top layer has a shark tooth fossil. How did this area change over time?

items.e: Bottom layers are older. The tree leaf (older) shows dry land; the shark tooth (younger) shows covered by ocean.

items.q: Why should you not hammer cliffs to find fossils?
c: It is dangerous and can cause rocks to fall.
items.e: Look on the beach instead.

items.q: Why do old gravestones made of limestone become hard to read?
c: Rain slowly wears away the soft rock.

items.e: Weathering.

items.q: Joy finds a fossil fish in a layer and a fossil fern in the layer just above it. Which happened first?
items.e: The lower layer is older.

items.q: Bianca models rock layers with colored sand in a jar. Which color did she pour first?
items.e: The first layer poured ends up on the bottom.

items.q: The rock layers have not been turned over. Which layer is the oldest?
